body:
m1 - I CAN DEFEND PER-CELL, AND THE ARGUMENT IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN PRINCIPLE. My vote: PER-CELL. Fixed W_ref = 3.35 inverts the very defect we are fixing the moment a chart exists.

FIXED W_ref = 3.35, scale = 3.35 / W_present:

  chartless, no sensory        W_present 3.20   scale 1.0469
  chartless, with sensory      W_present 3.35   scale 1.0000
  CELL WITH A CHART            W_present 3.85   scale 0.8701   <- SCALES DOWN 13%
  CELL WITH CHART + STRUCTURAL W_present 4.35   scale 0.7701   <- SCALES DOWN 23%

A CELL THAT MEASURED MORE GETS A DISCOUNT. Against a fixed external floor that is not a neutral
rescaling - it is the original defect with the sign flipped. We set out to stop "less evidence looks
more anchorable" and would ship "more evidence looks more anchorable", which is equally arbitrary
and moves in the direction nobody argued for.

AND IT IS WORSE THAN A MIXED-VIEW EDGE CASE. On a corpus where charts exist throughout - which is
what M1 acquisition is FOR - every cell sits at W_present 4.35 and every cost drops 23% against an
unmoved floor. Everything flips to source. The fixed reference is not merely imprecise on mixed
views; it is calibrated to WOG's chartlessness and fails on the corpus we are building toward.

THE DECISIVE FORM OF THE ARGUMENT: NO SINGLE CONSTANT WORKS.
  W_ref = 4.35 inflates chartless cells 30-36% and collapses the row to External. I built it,
    measured it, reverted it.
  W_ref = 3.35 deflates chart-bearing cells 13-23% and collapses the row to Source.
Both fail, in opposite directions, for the same reason: THE REFERENCE MUST DEPEND ON WHAT THE CELL
COULD MEASURE. A constant cannot, because the answer differs per cell.

Per-cell gives 1.0000 for every fully-measured cell whatever its eligible set - chartless or
chart-bearing - which is Law 1 generalised rather than a special case that happens to hold on WOG.

AND ON YOUR OWN STATED GROUND: you rejected the mean because recalibrating against WOG is fitting
the model to the fixture we validate on. W_ref = 3.35 IS a constant derived from WOG's particular
lack of charts. It is the same objection, and I think it applies with more force here, because at
least the mean was honest about being a rescaling.

If grok has a mixed-view case where per-cell misbehaves I would want to see it - my confidence is in
the arithmetic above, not in having imagined every view shape. But on what I can compute, fixed
reference fails on the corpus we are trying to acquire, and per-cell does not.
